title: Evolutionary insights and structural characterization guide the development of RAG1/RAG2-deficient swine models for immunological research.
authors: Zhang, Rui; Wu, Yunpeng; Sun, Tianqi; Luan, Tianqi; Ren, Yanling; Zhang, Yilin; Lin, Lihao; Meng, Teng; Wang, Jin; Qiu, Yefeng
one_liner_zh: 该文通过进化分析和结构建模表征猪RAG1/RAG2并构建基因敲除猪模型，虽涉及蛋白结构预测与对接，但核心是免疫缺陷动物模型开发，非TF-DNA结合互作研究，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Defects in RAG1/RAG2-mediated V(D)J recombination cause severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID), a disorder characterized by the absence of mature T and B lymphocytes resulting from impaired antigen receptor gene rearrangement. Although evolutionary analyses demonstrate strong conservation of the catalytic core domains of RAG1/RAG2 across jawed vertebrates, structural divergence among species highlights the need for physiologically relevant large-animal models to evaluate human disease mechanisms. Pigs represent an advantageous model for human pathologies because of their close immunological and physiological similarities to humans. METHODS: In this study, we performed evolutionary profiling, conservation analysis, tertiary structural modeling, and protein docking to characterize pig RAG1 and RAG2 and predict their functional roles in V(D)J recombination. These predictions were experimentally validated through the generation of RAG1 and RAG2 knockout pigs using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing. RESULTS: Our findings define key structural features of pig RAG1 and RAG2 that are essential for V(D)J recombination and establish an integrated framework that combines comprehensive computational analyses with in vivo experimental validation. DISCUSSION: This approach supports the development of pigs as physiologically relevant models of RAG deficiency and provides a foundation for future studies in pig immunology, genome editing, and translational research. Furthermore, these immunodeficient pigs permit long-term engraftment of human tissue xenografts and stem cell-derived teratomas, thereby enabling investigations of human immune reconstitution, cancer biology, and regenerative medicine. Collectively, this model offers a robust platform for immunotherapy development and for advancing studies in evolutionary and comparative immunology research.
abstract_zh: 引言：RAG1/RAG2介导的V(D)J重组缺陷导致严重联合免疫缺陷（SCID），这是一种以成熟T和B淋巴细胞缺失为特征的疾病，其根源在于抗原受体基因重排受损。尽管进化分析表明RAG1/RAG2的催化核心结构域在有颌脊椎动物中高度保守，但物种间的结构差异凸显了建立生理相关的大动物模型以评估人类疾病机制的必要性。猪因其与人类在免疫学和生理学上的高度相似性，成为研究人类病理学的优势模型。方法：在本研究中，我们进行了进化谱系分析、保守性分析、三级结构建模和蛋白质对接，以表征猪RAG1和RAG2并预测其在V(D)J重组中的功能角色。这些预测通过使用CRISPR/Cas9介导的基因组编辑生成RAG1和RAG2敲除猪进行了实验验证。结果：我们的研究结果定义了猪RAG1和RAG2中对V(D)J重组至关重要的关键结构特征，并建立了一个整合综合计算分析与体内实验验证的集成框架。讨论：该方法支持将猪发展为RAG缺陷的生理相关模型，并为未来猪免疫学、基因组编辑和转化研究奠定基础。此外，这些免疫缺陷猪允许人类组织异种移植物和干细胞来源畸胎瘤的长期植入，从而促进对人类免疫重建、癌症生物学和再生医学的研究。总体而言，该模型为免疫治疗开发以及推进进化与比较免疫学研究提供了强有力的平台。
